ownership_reason: Only the gold sees an escape sequence and the two characters that follow the escape character; hops 1-4 hold the whole array and the buffer and never an individual escape. Once the gold has folded Character.digit's -1 into an octet ("=WW" written as 0xEF), no caller can tell it from a genuine "=EF", so the effect cannot be recovered after the gold. The convention is pinned outside the gold: URLCodec.decodeUrl decodes its escapes the same way and sends both characters through Utils.digit16, which throws DecoderException for a character that is not a hexadecimal digit (URLCodecTest::testDecodeInvalid: "%WW" and "%0W" throw); Hex.decodeHex checks every character with Hex.toDigit (HexTest::testDecodeBadCharacterPos0 / Pos1: "q0" and "0q" throw); Utils.digit16 is what the facade's original body used. The gold's javadoc promises the octets represented by the quoted-printable characters, which "=WW" does not have, and the facade's javadoc promises DecoderException when quoted-printable decoding is unsuccessful. A hop that pre-validates the whole array with a regular expression passes the existing tests but is a second implementation of the gold's per-escape decision at a level that never sees an escape (recorded bypass).
